We need to indicate number of C=O groups in the molecule. We need the molecule structure. Not provided directly. We may need to get IR spectra to see carbonyl stretch? Or carbon NMR? But easiest is to get IR spectra which shows C=O stretch around 1700 cm-1. However counting groups from IR may be ambiguous. Perhaps we can get carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-220 ppm). But we need the molecule. There is no SMILES given. Maybe the sample at hand is predetermined. We need to measure IR to detect carbonyl groups. Use ir_spectra tool. That will give a string with peaks. We can count number of carbonyl peaks. Usually each carbonyl gives a strong peak near 1700. If multiple carbonyls, may have multiple peaks. Could also be overlapping. But we can assume each distinct carbonyl gives a peak.

Thus we should call ir_spectra.
